_comment: Default landing page: ONE answer key, four frameworks. Feature 46.
LAND-DEC-01 (ratify dev-only): the built-in welcome page at GET / is
DEV-ONLY (TINA4_DEBUG truthy) in all four - production always 404s. This
was already the shipped behaviour; a prior-session audit doc had left
production unverified and RECOMMENDED 'allow it in production', which
would reopen a fingerprinting leak (the page exposes the framework
version, a /__dev admin link, and a gallery). That recommendation is
REJECTED here - the 404-in-prod info-leak guard is now end-to-end-gated
by a REAL GET / in all four (previously only Ruby and Node proved it
end-to-end; Python and PHP asserted only the TINA4_DEBUG flag helper).
LAND-DEC-02 (maintainability + parity, low priority): unify the
suppression precedence and delete dead code.
- Suppression precedence, unified across all four: a user-registered
GET / route wins outright; failing that, a src/templates/pages/
index.* template wins over the landing page; failing that, the page
renders in dev / 404s in production. PHP and Python already did
this. Node's request-time fallback chain already ran the template
stage before the landing stage. Ruby's WORKING template-auto-routing
path (#resolve_template / #try_serve_template, called first inside
#handle_404) ALREADY resolved src/templates/pages/index.* - verified
empirically before writing this fixture (a real RackApp#call with a
real pages/index.twig on disk returns 200 with the template body and
no landing banner). Ruby's SEPARATE should_show_landing_page? /
try_serve_index_template pair checked a DIFFERENT, never-wired
convention (src/templates/index.* - no pages/ subdirectory) and was
unreferenced in the main checkout (a stray uncommitted worktree still
called it - not the working tree this fixture was proven against).
So Ruby needed NO suppression fix, only the dead-code deletion below,
plus a real test proving the (already-correct) precedence.
- Dead code deleted, not wired: Node's renderLandingPage(routes, port)
never referenced routes (server.ts) yet the caller built
ctx.router.getRoutes().map(...) on EVERY request that reaches the
fallback chain and threw the result away - deleted the parameter and
the wasted per-request map(). Ruby's should_show_landing_page? and
try_serve_index_template (see above) were deleted outright.
LAND-MECHANISM-DIVERGE (documented, not converged - low priority per the
ledger): PHP REGISTERS the landing page as a bootstrap route inside
App::start() (registerLandingPage(), only when dev AND no user / route
AND no pages/index.* template) - it is a real entry in the route table.
Python, Ruby and Node instead serve it from a REQUEST-TIME FALLBACK (no-
route / 404 handler / FALLBACK_STAGES) that runs only when nothing
matched. Observable behaviour converges (proven by this fixture); the
mechanism does not, and the ledger does not require forcing convergence.
This is also why the PHP suite below drives the REAL App::start() boot
path (TestClient alone would never see the bootstrap-registered route),
while Python/Ruby/Node dispatch a real GET / with no separate boot step.
Every case is driven through a REAL request pipeline - Python's
TestClient (core.server.app), PHP's real Tina4\App::start() bootstrap +
TestClient (Router::dispatch - the only way to exercise PHP's actual
mechanism), Ruby's TestClient-equivalent RackApp#call, and Node's real
startServer() over a real HTTP socket - NO mocks anywhere. Positive AND
negative cases; the production-leak case is mutation-proved (temporarily
dropping the dev gate in each language's source turns it RED, restoring
the gate turns it back green) as part of implementing this fixture.
The four suites carry the SAME case names in each language's own idiom
(Python snake_case function, PHP testPascalCase method, Ruby it-
description, Node assert label), which scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py
normalises and matches.

invariants.rule: With TINA4_DEBUG truthy and no user GET / route, a real GET / returns 200 and the body contains the branded banner (the framework's own title - Tina4Python/Tina4Php/Tina4Ruby/Tina4NodeJs).
invariants.why: The whole point of the feature: a fresh app shows a branded welcome page in dev so a developer sees the framework is running.

invariants.rule: With TINA4_DEBUG falsy, a real GET / returns 404, and the body carries NONE of: the branded banner, the framework version string, a /__dev link, or the gallery section - in all four. This is the SECURITY case (LAND-PROD-DECIDED): the page would otherwise fingerprint the framework version and expose a dev-admin link to a production caller. REJECTS the prior-session doc's 'allow it in production' recommendation, which would reopen exactly this leak.
invariants.why: LAND-PROD-DECIDED / LAND-TEST-PARITY: production behaviour was previously end-to-end-gated in only Ruby and Node (Python and PHP asserted the TINA4_DEBUG flag helper only, never the actual / response) - a regression here would have shipped silently in two of four languages.

invariants.rule: A user-registered GET / handler always answers a real GET / instead of the landing page or a 404 - in BOTH dev and production, in all four.
invariants.why: The landing page must never shadow a real app's own homepage; this is the precedence a default app depends on the moment it defines its own /.

invariants.rule: When the app ships src/templates/pages/index.* (twig/html), a real GET / serves THAT template's content (200) instead of the landing page - in dev, in all four, now unified (Ruby's already-correct #resolve_template/#try_serve_template precedence proven here for the first time; its separate DEAD should_show_landing_page?/try_serve_index_template pair, which checked an unwired src/templates/index.* convention, is deleted rather than wired - see LAND-SUPPRESS-DIVERGE).
invariants.why: LAND-SUPPRESS-DIVERGE: the prior doc believed Ruby lacked this suppression entirely (reading only the dead, unreferenced pair) - unproven and, per a real dispatch, false. Every framework must let a project's own pages/index.* win over the framework's own welcome page, matching the Next.js/Nuxt-style pages/ convention the auto-router already uses everywhere else.
